preemption.details: California does not have statewide preemption for knife laws. Local municipalities (e.g., Los Angeles, San Francisco) may enact stricter knife ordinances than state law.

open_carry.details: Open carry of most knives is generally legal in California. Folding knives of any blade length may be carried openly. Fixed-blade knives must be carried in a sheath worn openly suspended from the waist.

statutes.title: Carrying concealed dirk or dagger prohibited

concealed_carry.details: Concealed carry depends on the type of knife. Folding knives (non-locking and locking) may generally be carried concealed. Dirks, daggers, and fixed-blade knives cannot be concealed. A 'dirk or dagger' is broadly defined as any knife or instrument capable of ready use as a stabbing weapon that may inflict great bodily injury or death.

blade_length.details: California does not impose a statewide blade length limit. However, local ordinances may restrict blade length (e.g., Los Angeles restricts concealed carry of knives with blades over 3 inches).

switchblade.details: Switchblades with a blade of 2 inches or longer are illegal to carry, possess in a vehicle, sell, or otherwise transfer. Switchblades with a blade shorter than 2 inches are legal.

automatic.details: Automatic knives fall under the switchblade definition in California. If the blade is 2 inches or longer and opens automatically, it is illegal.

assisted_opening.details: Assisted-opening knives are generally legal in California. They are distinguished from switchblades because the user must apply manual force to begin opening the blade.

ballistic_knife.details: Ballistic knives are prohibited under both federal law and California Penal Code.

restricted_locations.summary: Schools (K-12 and colleges), government buildings, courts, airports, and other locations as defined by statute.
restricted_locations.details: It is illegal to bring any knife with a blade longer than 2.5 inches onto K-12 school grounds. Possession of weapons on state or local public buildings and at public meetings is also restricted.

statutes.title: Weapons in state or local public buildings
